learning_outcomes.text: Understand the behavior of elastic materials: stresses and strains. Know the fundamentals of strength of materials and the principles of beam theory.
Be able to calculate internal forces in beam-type structural elements.
Calculate the stresses existing in a cross-section of a structural element.
Perform the dimensioning of beams working in bending and simple metallic joints.
Perform the study of deformations in isostatic structures.
Analyze the degree of hyperstaticity or mechaniccity of a structure. Solve beam theory problems with ease, up to a hyperstaticity degree of 2.
Know material failure modes and criteria.

syllabus_topics: Basic concepts and hypotheses of Strength of Materials.
Study of deformations in isostatic structures.
Resolution of hyperstatic structures in flexibility.
assessment_rules: To pass, a minimum total score of 5 out of 10 is required. Voluntary practices can add up to 1 point to the final exam score, reducing the minimum required exam score to 4.00 if all practices are successfully completed. A partial exam (Block I, max 5 points) can be taken; if 2.5 points or more are obtained, the score is kept, and only Block II (max 5 points) is assessed in the final exam. If the full final exam (Block I + Block II, max 10 points) is taken, the partial exam score is annulled; it is necessary to correctly answer at least one question from each block of the final exam.
